subject: DPF technical measures & control evidence request — Solaris Health / Redwood
messages:
From: Jen Rivers <j.rivers@solarischealth.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@solarischealth.com
Date: Fri, 14 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: DPF evidence and technical measures request

Hi Soojin,

Thanks for the demo last week — Solaris Health is moving quickly on our vendor review. Our legal and security teams have asked for a concise technical package to complete a Data Processing Framework (DPF) assessment before we can progress to contracting. Specifically we need:

- A control matrix mapping each DPF clause to concrete technical/organizational controls you have in place (encryption in transit/rest, KMS usage, access controls, logging retention, incident response).
- Example evidence for the controls (redacted audit-log extract, sample network diagram, encryption key rotation policy excerpt).
- Confirmation of lawful basis for EU->US processing and which transfer mechanism you will use.
- Any subcontractors/third parties that will see customer data and their geographic locations.

Can you provide this package by EOD Aug 20? We are on a tight timeline. Also please include any limitations on sharing raw logs (we can accept redacted extracts).

Thanks,
Jen
Jen Rivers
Head of Security Programs, Solaris Health

(415) 555-0192

Thanks for the heads-up, team. A couple of operational notes to make the package faster and safe to share externally:

- For audit logs we will provide timestamped extracts with all user identifiers hashed and internal hostnames replaced with generic labels (e.g., compute-node-1).
- KMS details: we can provide Cloud KMS/Azure Key Vault usage details and rotation cadence. We cannot share customer key material — we will provide policy excerpts and rotation audit entries.
- Transfer mechanism: we recommend the DPA Annex + SCCs for now and will include our DPF mapping that indicates the legal basis we rely on (Contract + legitimate interest as applicable) and a fallback to EU SCCs for EU customer processing.
- Subprocessors: we will include a table with subprocessors, their role, and regions (US/EU/APAC).

Soojin — please ensure all attachments have filenames that make redaction status obvious (e.g., redacted_audit_log_sample.csv). If Solaris needs unredacted evidence we will route that through an NDA/procurement-controlled SFTP and log every access.

Hannah

VP, Enterprise Sales Ops | Redwood Inference

Hi Jen / Procurement team —

Per our timeline, attaching the compiled package and links below. We redacted logs as discussed and included a clear control-to-evidence mapping. Summary of what we shared:

- Redwood_DPF_Control_Matrix_v1.xlsx 
  - Tab 1: DPF clause -> Redwood control mapping
  - Tab 2: Evidence pointers (file names & Drive links)
- redacted_audit_log_sample.csv (filtered, identifiers hashed)
- network_arch_diagram_public.pdf (high-level infra only)
- KMS_policy_excerpt.pdf (rotation cadence and vendor detail)
- DPA_Annex_Draft.docx (draft annex + suggested SCC addendum)

Links: https://drive.redwood.com/shared/solarischealth/dpf-package-8341
DocuSign (DPA annex signature): https://app.docusign.com/transactions/ABC1234567

Responses to procurement points:
- We do not proactively transfer PHI outside a customers configured region unless explicitly requested and contractually authorised. Transfers associated with managed services or subprocessor processing are listed in the subprocessor table (included in the workbook).
- Export controls: Our serving runtime does not embed restricted cryptographic technology beyond industry-standard TLS and KMS primitives. Model weights we ship are commercial open weights or customer-provided; if a customer needs FIPS/HSM-validated deployments we offer an on-prem/private deployment option.

If you need an SFTP with a signed NDA to review unredacted logs, we can provision that and log access. Otherwise let us know which items you want expanded or we can schedule a 45-minute technical walkthrough with our infra team.

Thanks,
Soojin Lee
